key_insight: A training-free rework of the SAM 3D Body inference pipeline—decoupling spatial dependencies and applying architecture-aware pruning—delivers interactive, real-time full-body mesh recovery without retraining the model.
problem_solved: SAM 3D Body is highly accurate but too slow (seconds per image) for real-time or interactive use; this work reduces inference latency to interactive rates while preserving accuracy.
method: Decouple serial spatial dependencies in the original pipeline to enable parallel processing of image regions.
Parallelized multi-crop feature extraction so multiple body-focused crops are computed concurrently instead of sequentially.
Apply architecture-aware pruning and streamline transformer decoding to remove redundant computation while maintaining mesh quality.
impact: Enables deployment of state-of-the-art 3D human mesh recovery in real-time applications (AR/VR, live animation, motion capture) without costly retraining or hardware changes, increasing practical usability for researchers and engineers.
visual_elements: Before vs After pipeline diagram: original serial SAM 3D Body flow (slow) vs Fast SAM 3D Body parallelized flow (fast).
Latency comparison bar chart: seconds-per-frame for baseline vs Fast SAM 3D Body across hardware targets.
Architecture schematic highlighting: multi-crop parallel extraction, pruned transformer blocks, and decoder simplification.
Qualitative panel: input images with overlaid predicted 3D meshes at real-time frame rates (video frame thumbnails).
paper_title: Fast SAM 3D Body: Accelerating SAM 3D Body for Real-Time Full-Body Human Mesh Recovery
paper_authors: Timing Yang, Sicheng He, Hongyi Jing, Jiawei Yang, Zhijian Liu
